title: Plant Parts and Needs
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Plant Parts and Needs Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the basic needs of plants; identify the major parts of plants and their functions; describe how water and nutrients move through a plant. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Growth and Changes in Plants)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on the parts of a plant, what plants need to grow and how water moves through plants. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Plants need light, air, water and nutrients.
key_sub: Roots take in water, stems carry it, leaves make food and flowers make seeds.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants need light, air, water, nutrients and space to grow.

  • Roots take in water and nutrients and hold the plant in the soil.
  • The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
  • Leaves use sunlight to make food. Flowers make seeds.
Example

Which part takes in water?

it is under the ground

Answer: the roots

Example

A plant is kept in the dark. What happens?

it cannot make food

Answer: it becomes pale and weak

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking all plants need the same amount of water.
  • Thinking roots only hold the plant up.

faq.q: What do plants need to grow?
faq.a: Light, air, water, nutrients from the soil and space.
Leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food for the plant.

faq.q: How does water get to the leaves?
faq.a: Water goes in through the roots and travels up the stem to the leaves.

to use sunlight to make food
to make seeds so new plants can grow
items.e: Part D points to the stem. This part holds the plant up and carries water and food.

items.q: Mei stood a Chinese cabbage leaf in a jar of water with purple food colouring. When the stem is cut across, what will Mei see?
c: small purple dots, which are the ends of the water tubes

items.e: The tubes carry the water up the stem.

items.q: Why does a plant droop (wilt) when it does not get enough water?
c: There is not enough water in the stem and leaves to keep them firm.
items.e: Water keeps plants firm.

items.q: Maya stood a Chinese cabbage leaf in a jar of water with purple food colouring. Where will the purple colour appear after a day?
c: only at the bottom of the stem
the thin lines (veins) in the leaf
nowhere, the colour stays in the jar
items.e: The coloured water travels up the stem to the top of the plant.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Where does it go after the leaves and flowers?
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Why do leaves feel cooler than the air on a hot day?
c: Water evaporating from them cools them down.
items.e: Like sweat.

items.q: Aiden stood a white lily in a jar of water with green food colouring. Why does the colour spread up the plant?
c: The plant takes up the coloured water through tiny tubes in its stem.
The colour floats up through the air.
items.e: The tubes carry water up from the bottom.

items.q: A tree is very tall. How does water reach the top leaves?
